articles.title: 'I Don't Fully Understand the Plot': Alan Cumming Can't Explain Avengers: Doomsday, But Reveals He Was Required to Lie On Top of Florence Pugh's Black Widow
articles.summary: X-Men star Alan Cumming has admitted he "didn't fully understand" the plot of Avengers: Doomsday while filming his scenes — one of which involved getting close to Florence Pugh's Black Widow.
body: If this latest tidbit from the Traitors host sounds familiar, it's because Cumming has leaked snippets about his time on Marvel's set previously — lamenting that his returning character Nightcrawler was filmed mostly against blue screen, and noting that he had got to fight Pedro Pascal's Reed Richards.

Now, Cumming has told SiriusXM (via Variety ) that he did have bits of Doomsday's story explained to him — only for him to respond that he didn't really need to know the plot as he was simply there to "run around."
Cumming also revealed that he had to, at one point, lie on top of Florence Pugh's Black Widow character — even though it was her stunt double that he actually laid upon.

"There was a bit when we were shooting a scene, and it was one of the rare scenes when I was actually on the backlot and not in front of a blue screen," Cumming began. "And this man came and said, 'So right now Alan, these giant robots are blah blah,' and started to tell me the thing, and I was like, 'You know what, thank you so much, but just tell me where I point my, whatever I point. And I'll do that. Really, I just know I'm here to run around'."
points: X-Men star Alan Cumming has admitted he "didn't fully understand" the plot of Avengers: Doomsday while filming his scenes — one of which involved getting close to Florence Pugh's Black Widow.

articles.title: Reacher Season 6 Confirmed While Season 5 Is Still in Production
articles.summary: There’s no end to Reacher in sight, after Amazon green lit Season 6 while Season 5 is still in production. Variety reported that Reacher Season 4, whose season finale hit Prime Video earlier this month, reached a whopping 66 million viewers within 28 days of launch.
body: Reacher star Alan Ritchson, whose popularity has exploded alongside the show, is currently filming Season 5 in Toronto. The series is an adaptation of Lee Child’s Jack Reacher book series, with each season loosely based on a particular novel. Amazon has yet to say which book Season 6 is based on.

While each season so far has varied in quality (Season 1 remains the high point for me), Reacher’s enormous popularity continues regardless. I imagine Amazon will want the 43-year-old Ritchson breaking bones for as long as his own can withstand the intense work schedule and fitness routine required for the role.

Meanwhile, Ritchson is among many names touted for various DC Universe and MCU roles. While he’s ruled out playing Batman for James Gunn, Ritchson has teased talks with the DC Studios co-CEO about potentially playing another character. He has the size to play any number of hulking superheroes or villains. Aquaman? Shazam? Captain Atom? Hawkman?

articles.title: Naughty Dog Is Working On Two New The Last Of Us Projects
articles.summary: Naughty Dog studio head Neil Druckmann has dropped some tantalizing news for fans of The Last of Us, confirming the studio is currently working on not one, but two new The Last of Us projects.
body: The Last of Us Day is marked on September 26, the day that was the start of the zombie apocalypse in the game's lore, and Naughty Dog celebrated the 2026 event with a charity livestream, fan giveaways, and new collaborations. The studio also launched new official The Last of Us social media accounts, hinting that our time with the franchise is far from over.

In a brief post reflecting on the day, studio head Neil Druckmann dropped a few major announcements for Naughty Dog's future, chief among them that there are two new The Last of Us projects currently in the early stages of development. "Both projects will expand the canon of The Last of Us beyond Part 1 and Part 2, Druckmann said. "The world of The Last of Us means a great deal to us, and we wouldn’t return to it unless we had something meaningful to say. We believe these stories are worth telling."

It's not clear whether either of the games will be The Last of Us Part 3, and we're unlikely to find out for some time--Druckman added that both projects are in very early stages, so details are locked down tight.

articles.title: All versions of The Witcher 3 "that exist in the world" will be upgraded with the free Remastered edition today
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red has clarified to Eurogamer that "all versions of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt that exist in the world" are to be updated with the free Remastered edition upgrade today. That update, by the way, rolls out from 11am BST.
body: Said CDPR in a statement: "As of today, all versions of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt that exist in the world - Complete, Game of the Year, and even the base game - will all become this new standard version that includes Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine by default. When The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered launches, all copies on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC will be upgraded for free."

Confirmation comes alongside a list of detailed patch notes for the Remastered update, which clarify a wide array of alterations to the game as well as document specific changes to PC, PlayStation and Switch 2 platforms (there don't appear to be any Xbox-specific changes of note, besides the game now being an Xbox Play Anywhere title).

articles.title: Sony is introducing an anti-scalping lottery system for PS5 Pros in Japan as supply shortages persist
articles.summary: Sony is introducing a lottery system for PS5 Pros on its Japanese online store for when demand for new consoles outstrips the limited supply.
body: As seen in a new information page on the official Sony website, a post confirms that Sony has begun accepting applications for PS5 Pro purchases.
To apply, you need a Sony account registered in Japan, and have played for more than 60 hours on that account over the past two years. Both appear to be scalping prevention measures, which is great.

Prospective buyers have from today until the 7th October to apply. Here comes the fun part: if the number of applications is larger than the available supply of PS5 Pros, the lottery will be held. Winners will be picked from applicants and messaged on the 26th October. Only these select few will have the pleasure of spending ¥137,980 (around £662 / $876) on a video game console.

Once selected you must hurry. If you don't drop a fat stack of cash within a week you'll lose your chance, and that PS5 Pro will escape your grasp, being thrown back into the lottery pool for another prospective buyer to claim.

articles.title: Xbox Disc-to-Digital Program Keeps Getting Larger, Adding Big Publisher
articles.summary: Xbox 's disc-to-digital feature is currently in its testing phase and is only available to those who are part of the Insiders program. This allows the company to receive feedback and release updates to ensure that disc-to-digital is in the best shape before public release.
body: The disc-to-digital program has been available to Xbox Insiders since Aug. 31. Its release didn't come as a surprise, as a roadmap outlining the feature was leaked shortly before. The program allows players to claim a digital license for games they physically own. This allows them to easily access the games as long as the license is associated with their account.

Since its release, Insiders have gotten acquainted with the program, sharing new details on it with the community and sending Xbox feedback to continue improving it. One of the best features of disc-to-digital is that it includes delisted games with previously unobtainable digital licenses. On the other hand, some titles that players expected to digitize easily, as they were widely available on digital platforms, couldn't be claimed because their publishers were not participating in the disc-to-digital program.

articles.title: How to Finally Get Over the Urge to Restart BG3
articles.summary: Nearly half of Baldur’s Gate 3 runs never make it past the game’s first act. That’s not to say half of the game’s players have never seen Act 2, necessarily: Steam’s data includes copies bought in a sale and never opened, and some mods disable achievement tracking, for example.
body: Ask why this is the case on the game’s subreddit and the community will instantly clue you in: “The game has only been out three years. Some of us don’t want to rush through character creation.” (Honestly, same.) Many of us do see starting Baldur’s Gate 3 over again as an extremely legitimate substitute for finishing the game in the first place…which likely tracks with anyone who’s ever fallen in love with a new character idea mid-run and abandoned a perfectly good save file in pursuit of shiny object syndrome.

Don’t worry. The character creator isn’t going anywhere. It’ll still be there for you if you do decide to abandon your current save file for another build. But what’s at stake here is everything that happens after most people, statistically, quit: Shadowheart’s actual reason for hiding a holy symbol, for instance…or whatever ’s waiting for your current party underneath Moonrise Towers. Give the run you’re already in the one thing restart-itis never allows: A true ending, even a messy one, instead of one more perfect beginning.

articles.title: In another unprecedented move, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is changing double XP tokens so they count down in match and not real-time
articles.summary: Just days after announcing a silly skin off toggle for Call of Duty: Warzone, Activision has returned to share some even better news for Modern Warfare 4. At launch and beyond, double XP tokens will count down only when you're actively in a match, not in real-world time.
body: Call of Duty's official X account delivered the news succinctly, confirming that existing tokens - ones you may have accrued from previous COD titles or Warzone - will also be usable in Modern Warfare 4.

Previously, activating a double XP token would begin the countdown immediately. If you need to get up from your chair, take too long building a loadout or idle as you wait for a friend to join, all that time will be wasted as tokens continue to deplete in the background. It's something that's been universally disliked for obvious reasons, and players have called on Activision to change the way it works with each new yearly COD release.

The issue also isn't exclusive to Call of Duty; rival franchise Battlefield treats double XP tokens the same way, and its community is similarly frustrated. Battlefield Studios recently made players even more upset by sending an in-game message promising to change tokens so they count down in-match, before saying it was an error - twice.

articles.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Movie Is So Popular, It Increased RE2 Remake Sales by More Than 50% on PS5
articles.summary: Data shows that Zach Cregger’s film adaptation of Capcom’s flagship horror franchise was so successful, it boosted sales for copies of both Resident Evil 2 Remake and RE4’s 2023 remake on the PlayStation 5.
body: Cregger’s Resident Evil has enjoyed resounding success on all fronts; not only is it the single most-profitable Resident Evil movie ever made, it’s also helping sales for the games it’s based on.

Stats aggregated by Alinea Analytics show that the Resident Evil 2 Remake and Resident Evil 4 (2023) enjoyed a massive boost in the week after Cregger’s movie hit theaters. As told in a substack post written by Alinea Analytics’ Rhys Elliot, RE2 remake and RE 4 (2023) enjoyed a whopping 64% and 54% increase in PS5 sales, respectively. With Steam copies added to the mix, the games got bumped up by an additional 11% and 14%, respectively.

On PlayStation, this means the two games’ revenue increased by a jaw-dropping 80% and 84%, though it’s also worth noting that Capcom slashed prices for the games about 10 days before Cregger’s movie hit theaters.

Elliot points out that, while deep discounts made up for most of these impressive numbers beforehand, Austin Abrams’ deeply relatable performance as Bryan moved the needle quite a bit in the week afterwards, which also translated to increased player numbers.

articles.title: How to get unlocked Multi Frame Gen working on an RTX 40-series graphics card
articles.summary: Jess has been writing about games for over ten years, spending a significant chunk of that time working on print publications PLAY and Official PlayStation Magazine.
body: Just in case you've been napping under a cool mossy rock since about January 2025, Multi Frame Generation (or MFG) is a frame rate boosting/game smoothing feature that leverages AI to create as many as five frames for every actually rendered frame. Nvidia introduced the original 2x Frame Generation feature with the RTX 40-series graphics cards in 2022. Sadly Nvidia restricted the more recent Multi Frame Generation version of the tech to RTX 50-series cards alone. Mmm, buttery; boo, proprietary.

As such, CEO Jensen Huang has said in the past that bringing "the latest generation AI technology to the previous generation GPUs" is a good idea but that it would " require a fair amount of engineering."

articles.title: This new super-bright 500 nit 'inkjet' tech promises to fix OLED's full-screen brightness limitation
articles.summary: Ignoring the teensy tiny issue of burn-in, there's one remaining limitation afflicting large OLED displays including PC monitors. Yup, it's full-screen brightness. But now there's a new OLED panel tech that promises to fix that with a full-screen capability of fully 500 nits.
body: The new OLED panel is from Chinese manufacturer TCL CSOT and is derived from technology first developed by now-defunct Japanese OLED specialist JOLED. We've already seen the first PC monitor based on the TCL CSOT's novel inkjet-print OLED panel from MSI. But now a new generation of the inkjet-based tech has already been announced and it's much brighter than before.

This panel tech from TCL CSOT is known as "inkjet" because the OLED material is "printed" onto the display substrate using a process akin to inkjet printers. That's in contrast to the evaporation and metal-mask deposition techniques typically used by Samsung and LG in existing OLED panels.

Showcased by Vincent from YouTube channel HDTV Test at the IFA 2026 event, the demo panel is a 27-inch 4K model running at 120 Hz. The first-generation inkjet OLED panel from TCL CSOT in the MSI Pro Max topped out at 300 nits for full-screen brightness. That's roughly on par with the latest QD-OLED and WOLED panels from Samsung and LG, which are capable of 300 nits and 335 nits respectively.

videos.summary: Sony has revealed a new image from the upcoming God of War Laufey, featuring Kratos. While Kratos appeared briefly in the game's extended gameplay trailer, this screenshot places Kratos and Laufey in what appears to be ancient Greece, from a time before they even met.
points: Sony has revealed a new image from the upcoming God of War Laufey, featuring Kratos.
While Kratos appeared briefly in the game's extended gameplay trailer, this screenshot places Kratos and Laufey in what appears to be ancient Greece, from a time before they even met.
Not much is known about the game's story and setting, aside from Laufey waking up in the Everywhen after being cremated by Kratos in the 2018 game.
And finally, Avengers: Endgame Encore assembled an impressive $86 million global box office haul in its first re-release.
videos.author: IGN

videos.title: DF Direct Weekly #283: Halo Moves To Activision, Next-Gen TFLOPs, Silent Hill Townfall Tested!
videos.summary: Thanks to Alienware for sponsoring DF Direct. To learn more about the Alienware AREA-51 Gaming Desktop, check out:
body: An extremely busy week at the Foundry but the Direct cannot be stopped - the team discuss the latest news as the "Xbox Reset" enters Phase Two and Halo is shipped off to Activision. Meanwhile, Rich, Oliver and Tom join forces to run the rule over Silent Hill Townfall, becauise the show moves on to discuss the implications of the next-gen consoles' respective GPU TFLOPs numbers. And finally, ending the show on a high note, Rich revisits 007 First Light path tracing, finding a night and day improvement in performance over the original release.
